Llevabas meses pidiéndole a tu mamá un <:
For months you'd been asking your mom for a professional drone, the kind with a 4K camera and GPS.

Today she shows up with a cardboard box and a smile: "Honey, I couldn't afford the one you wanted… but this one you build yourself. They say whoever builds it learns more."

Inside: a wooden drone in pieces, some simple motors, an ESP32 board, a toy camera… and a soldering iron.

Lo de abajo primero: motores y el stack: Bottom first: motors and the stack (ESC and flight controller) before the battery; what's on top covers what's below. To unmount, hold down on a mounted part.
Al <b>ESC</b>: la batería (XT60) y los 4: To the ESC: the battery (XT60) and the 4 motors. To the flight controller (the ESP32): the radio, the camera and the ESC plug. Each pad has its name printed; the tabs at the top switch boards.
1. Flux en el pad (<kbd>F</kbd>). 2. Cau:
1. Flux on the pad (F). 2. Iron on the pad (hold the click) to heat it. 3. Solder (Space): just a little. 4. Let go.
Too much solder = bridge (short); cold pad = cold joint. The bench doesn't warn you: you find out in the smoke test or with the multimeter.
Se ensucia con cada junta (la barrita de: It gets dirty with every joint (the bar at the bottom): clean it with <kbd>C</kbd>. Turn off the station ⏻ when done or it oxidizes.
